name: Andromeda Galaxy Well Placed
where: Look northeast, up from the Great Square of Pegasus toward Cassiopeia's 'W'; M31 sits about halfway between them
best_time: Late evening, once high in the sky
description: The Andromeda Galaxy (M31), 2.5 million light-years away, rides high on autumn nights. From a dark site it appears as an elongated smudge to the naked eye and reveals its bright core and dust lanes through binoculars or a telescope — a premier long-exposure astrophotography target.

name: Planetary Alignment
where: Look east along the ecliptic before sunrise; the planets form a line low across the dawn sky
description: Several bright planets gather along the ecliptic in the pre-dawn sky, strung out in a rough line. A wide-angle lens over a low eastern horizon captures the whole lineup — set an alarm for about 45 minutes before sunrise.
